title: Group DETR: Fast DETR Training with Group-Wise One-to-Many Assignment
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)

problem.summary: DETR's one-to-one assignment promotes only a single prediction per ground-truth object, which makes training slow to converge, while naively applying the one-to-many assignment used by Faster R-CNN/FCOS breaks DETR's duplicate-scoring mechanism; injecting one-to-many supervision into DETR training without losing NMS-free end-to-end inference remains unsolved.
statements: DETR supervises only the one prediction assigned to each ground-truth object and must actively demote all duplicates, so supervision per object is sparse.
Naive one-to-many assignment fails for DETR training because duplicate predictions have no scoring mechanism to demote them.
Slow DETR convergence motivates schemes that add supervision or stabilize the assignment.

evidence.quote: Detection transformer (DETR) relies on one-to-one assignment, assigning one ground-truth object to one prediction, for end-to-end detection without NMS post-processing.
While the naive one-to-many assignment does not work for DETR, and it remains challenging to apply one-to-many assignment for DETR training.
Unfortunately, naive one-to-many assignment does not work for DETR training.
It remains a challenge to apply one-to-many assignment to DETR training.

background.summary: The paper builds on DETR's bipartite set prediction and organizes prior acceleration work into two complementary lines: modifying cross-attention to sample informative regions (deformable attention, Conditional DETR, SMCA) and stabilizing one-to-one assignment (DN-DETR, DINO). One-to-many assignment so far only exists in non-end-to-end detectors that rely on NMS post-processing.

relatedWork.name: DETR
relatedWork.relation: base end-to-end detector relying on bipartite one-to-one matching
relatedWork.quote: DETR [4] relies on one-to-one assignment, where each ground-truth object is assigned to a single prediction through building a bipartite matching between the predictions and the ground-truth objects.

relatedWork.name: DN-DETR
relatedWork.relation: prior work that stabilizes one-to-one assignment with noisy queries
relatedWork.quote: DN-DETR [29] finds the assignment process is unstable and attributes the slow convergence issue to the instabilities.

relatedWork.name: Deformable DETR
relatedWork.relation: cross-attention modification line that samples informative positions
relatedWork.quote: Deformable attention [70] selects the highly informative positions dynamically according to the previous decoder embedding.

relatedWork.name: Faster R-CNN and FCOS
relatedWork.relation: non-end-to-end detectors where one-to-many assignment succeeds
relatedWork.quote: One ground-truth object is assigned to multiple anchors or multiple pixels.

evidence.quote: There are two main lines for accelerating DETR training: modify cross-attention and stabilize one-to-one assignment.
During inference, a post-processing NMS is conducted for duplicate detection removal.

solution.summary: Group DETR splits the object queries into K groups, performs one-to-one matching independently inside each group and computes decoder self-attention separately per group, so each ground-truth object receives multiple positives across groups; architecturally this equals parallel decoders sharing parameters, and inference uses a single group, keeping the model NMS-free with no architecture change.
solution.approach: Replicate object queries into K groups with one-to-one assignment inside each group and isolated self-attention, turning group-wise one-to-many supervision into extra training signal without changing inference.
components: K groups of object queries (K = 11 by default)
one-to-one bipartite matching conducted independently within each group
separate decoder self-attention per group to keep competition inside each group
parallel-decoder implementation with shared encoder/decoder/predictor parameters
single group of queries at inference, identical to normally trained DETR

evidence.quote: This approach involves using multiple groups of object queries, conducting one-to-one assignment within each group, and performing decoder self-attention separately.
Our approach adopts K groups of object queries, and introduces group-wise one-to-many assignment.
The inference process is the same as DETR trained normally and only needs one group of queries without any architecture modification.
Regarding inference, it is the same as DETR trained normally, and only needs a single group of object queries.

experiments.summary: Group DETR is layered on Conditional DETR, DAB-DETR, DN-DETR, DAB-Deformable-DETR and DINO with ResNet-50 on COCO train2017/val2017 under 12, 36 and 50-epoch schedules, plus nuScenes multi-view 3D detection, instance segmentation and a ViT-Huge COCO test-dev system; ablations isolate group-wise assignment, separate self-attention, group count and training-cost overhead.

benchmarks.split: val2017, Conditional DETR + Group DETR, 12 epochs, ResNet-50
val2017, DAB-DETR + Group DETR, 12 epochs, ResNet-50
test-dev, ViT-Huge foundation model with TTA

evidence.quote: It boosts Conditional DETR (-DC5) [41] by 5.0 (4.8) mAP, improves DAB-DETR (-DC5) [36] by 3.9 (4.4) mAP, and brings a 2.0 (2.6) mAP gain to DN-DETR (-DC5) [29].
When applying to DINO [65, 29, 70], Group DETR also exceeds it by 0.7 mAP.
Our model is the first to achieve 64.5 mAP on COCO test-dev.

limitations.summary: The extra groups add training-time computation and memory (about 1.2-1.7 GB more GPU memory and roughly 5 extra minutes per epoch), detection accuracy saturates once the group count reaches 11, and the large-model test-dev result still trails systems built with more pre-training data and larger backbones.
items: Group DETR raises training FLOPs and GPU memory relative to the baseline detector.
Detection performance stops improving once the number of groups reaches 11.
The 64.5 AP test-dev model is outperformed by EVA and InterImage-H, which use larger foundation models and more pre-training data.

evidence.quote: Group DETR will bring additional training computation costs (FLOPs) as well as training memory costs.
For example, with Conditional DETR [41] and DAB-DETR [36], the memory increases are just 1.2 G and 1.7 G (Figure 7).

Models such as EVA [15] and InterImage-H [56], with larger foundation models (ViT-giant [62] or InterImage-H [56]) and more data [13, 5, 47, 68, 51, 45], give higher results (64.7 mAP and 65.4 mAP) than our model.
The detection performance improves when increasing the number of groups, and becomes stable when the group number reaches 11.

futureDirections.direction: Push the 64.5 AP test-dev result further by scaling up pre-training data and model size.
futureDirections.quote: We expect that our results will be further improved with more pre-training data and larger models.

deploymentClaims: Inference uses a single group of queries with no architecture modification, so test-time cost equals normally trained DETR
